title: Personnel of the first downtown Cotton Club band, 1936
summary: Hinton and Thomas reconstruct the rhythm section, saxophones, trombones and trumpets of the 1936 band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: That was a great band. Remember the first band downtown in 1936? We went downtown in 1936 to the
Thomas - 124

Cotton Club. That's when Social Security started. We got out... Well, Social Security didn't start until 1937. But they gave us our cards. I have my original card in my pocket right now, a Social Security card from 1937.
I had mine originally. But I think I need a new one now.

Do you remember the guys in the band, can you (?) that band now...? Let's take the rhythm section first, since I'm in the rhythm section. I'll name the rhythm section. There was Benny Payne on piano, Morris White on guitar, Leroy Maxey on drums, and I was on bass. Now, you name a section.
Well, the saxophones had Hilton Jefferson... I'm trying to think of somebody else...
Andrew Brown. You know that.
Andrew Brown. Was Ben Webster in that band?
Ben Webster.
Ben Webster. I was on the other tenor.
What?
I was on the other tenor. We had two tenors. And was Blake on it?
Jerry Blake.
Jerry Blake was on baritone.
Thomas - 125

That was the first band to hit the Cotton Club downtown. The only man I would question would be Jerry Blake. Let's see, now. There was Hilton Jefferson, who had just joined the band... He joined the band a week before I did, because Garvin Bushell had just left. Bushell had got fired, and they got Jeff a week before I joined the band. So there was Hilton Jefferson, Walter Thomas, Andrew Brown...
We had another guy on baritone. I can't think of his name now.

Oh, I know. ..[INAUDIBLE NAME]..... But he wasn't there. Al Gibson, he wasn't there then. So Hilton Jefferson on alto; Andrew Brown on the second alto; Walter Thomas on the other tenor... I think Jerry Blake... Four saxophones, right?
Eddie Barefield was in there, wasn't he?
No, Eddie Barefield wasn't in the band.
Eddie wasn't in the band then.
He never worked with the band there.
Oh, he didn't?
No, he came up later. Now, the trombones were... There were three trombones. There were Claude Jones, Keg Johnson and DePriest Wheeler.
Right.
Thomas - 126
Now, the trumpet section was Lamar Wright, Doc Cheatham and Mouse Randolph.
I never did understand why they let Mouse go. Because Mouse was a good trumpet player.
He was a terrific trumpet player.
But we got somebody, Cab got somebody...
